title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: 𝒳 is a simplicial set and Δ/𝒳 is its category of simplices (its category of elements). The projection Δ/𝒳 → Δ, which Grothendieck labels 'fibration', is a discrete fibration with fibres the sets 𝒳_n.

Top of page, general lemma. For a fibration C → B with fibres C_b, a base morphism i: b' → b induces i^*: C_b → C_{b'}. For F on C (contravariant in the appropriate sense), the left Kan extension to B is computed fibrewise: b ↦ ⊕_{x∈C_b} F(x). The transition map sends the summand at x to the summand at i^*(x) via F(x) → F(i^*x). Dually, for the right Kan extension: b ↦ ∏_{x∈C_b} F(x), where the component at x is obtained by projecting onto i^*x and applying F(i^*x) → F(x). This works because, for an (op)fibration, the fibre is cofinal (resp. coinitial) in the relevant comma category.

Application. Let ℰ be a category with direct sums.
- A contravariant functor A_*: (Δ/𝒳)^op → ℰ is called a 'faisceau' on 𝒳: a system of coefficients contravariant in a variable simplex of 𝒳.
- To it one attaches the simplicial object C_*(𝒳, A_*) = i_!(A): Δ^op → ℰ, given by n ↦ ⊕_{x∈𝒳_n} A(x). Here i: (Δ/𝒳)^ → Δ^ is the étale ('induction') morphism of presheaf topoi, using (Δ/𝒳)^ ≃ Δ^/𝒳.
- Dually, for ℰ with products, a covariant A^*: Δ/𝒳 → ℰ (a 'cofaisceau') gives the cosimplicial object C^*(𝒳, A^*): n ↦ ∏_{x∈𝒳_n} A(x).

Grothendieck remarks that replacing ℰ by ℰ^op reduces one case to the other. He also notes that the construction commutes with composition by functors ℰ → ℰ' preserving sums (resp. products).

These are simplicial chains with local or twisted coefficients and cochains with coefficients in a functor on the simplex category. They serve, presumably, as a technical tool for Čech/simplicial resolutions in the divided-power de Rham / crystalline notes.
errors: No mathematical error. The written-out product case is a little garbled: the right-hand arrows mix up x, x' and i^*(x'). The correct rule is that the component at x of the map ∏_{C_{b'}} → ∏_{C_b} is pr_{i^*x} followed by A(i^*x) → A(x).
Calling Δ/𝒳 → Δ a 'fibration' is correct (it is a discrete fibration). The sum formula for i_! uses that its opposite is an opfibration, which is the case here.

ideas.what: Left/right Kan extension along a (discrete) fibration is computed fibrewise as sums/products over the fibres.
ideas.modern_name: Pointwise Kan extension along (op)fibrations; final fibre inclusion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Gabriel–Zisman 1967; folklore; SGA 4 for fibred topoi)
ideas.where_published: Related material appears in SGA 4 (exposés on fibred categories and topoi) and later in Les Dérivateurs; the exact statement here is unsure.

ideas.what: Simplicial chains C_*(𝒳, A) and cosimplicial cochains C^*(𝒳, A) of a simplicial set with coefficients in a functor on its category of simplices, defined as i_! / i_* along the étale morphism Δ^/𝒳 → Δ^.
ideas.modern_name: Homology/cohomology of simplicial sets with local (or functor) coefficients; chains with coefficients in a presheaf on the simplex category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabriel–Zisman (1967, Appendix II); also Quillen; Baues–Wirsching (1985) for categories
ideas.where_published: Similar coefficient formalism appears in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs; the exact formulation is unsure.

ideas.what: Duality via ℰ ↔ ℰ^op, and compatibility of the construction with functors preserving sums or products.
ideas.modern_name: Formal duality / naturality of Kan extensions

deep.surprise_reason: A standard scratch-page formalisation of simplicial chains and cochains with coefficients in a functor on Δ/𝒳, written as Kan extensions along a discrete fibration. It is well known and contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'morphisme d'inducation' should read 'morphisme d'induction (des topos induits)'.
'On peut se limiter à l'aide' should probably read 'On peut se limiter à l'un [des cas]', before 'en remplaçant ℰ par ℰ°'.
In the Σ diagram the right-hand target should be F(i^*(x)) (the summand at i^*x), not F(i(x')).
'(à droite)' is a marginal circled annotation, probably 'à droite', near the top-right of the diagram.
The mark '${}^t h$' next to the bottom vertical arrow is uncertain and is perhaps a crossed-out symbol; it is not part of the mathematics.
